## Why jellyqda

jellyqda is a small QDA (qualitative data analysis) tool that runs **entirely
offline inside RStudio**. No interview data ever leaves your laptop. All
project data lives in **one SQLite file per project** (`.jellyqda`) -- mobile,
git-friendly, readable in 20 years.

The key design decision: imported text is **frozen** into the database at
import time and never re-extracted. Character offsets in codings therefore
never drift.

## Data model

| table     | columns                                                        |
|-----------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `sources` | `id, name, format, frozen_text, meta_json`                     |
| `codes`   | `id, label, parent_id, color, description`                     |
| `codings` | `id, source_id, code_id, start, end, memo`                     |
| `memos`   | `id, text_, created_at`                                        |
| `events`  | `id, action, details, created_at` (audit trail)                |

`codings$start`/`end` are 1-based inclusive character offsets into
`sources$frozen_text`.

## Workflow

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(jellyqda)

qda_open("meinarbeit.jellyqda")                       # open or create project
qda_import(c("interview_01.docx", "feldnotizen.pdf")) # freeze texts
qda_code_add("Beruflicher Werdegang")              # deductive code
qda_code_add("KMU", parent = "Beruflicher Werdegang")

qda_view(1)                                        # transcript in the Viewer, numbered segments
qda_code(source = 1, segment = 3, code = "KMU", memo = "5 Jahre KMU")
qda_code(source = 1, start = 120, end = 340, code = "Beruflicher Werdegang") # or by offsets

qda_segments("KMU")                                # all passages with this code
qda_codes()                                        # codebook as a tree
qda_stats()                                        # progress: % coded
qda_export("all")                                  # segments/codebook/audit as files
qda_backup()                                       # timestamped zip outside the project folder
```

## Import formats

`.txt`, `.md`, `.docx` and `.pdf` are first-class. Text files are read as raw
bytes, the encoding is detected (`readr`/`stringi`) and everything is
normalized to UTF-8. `.docx` goes through `officer`, `.pdf` through
`pdftools`. A PDF without a usable text layer is imported with a warning; the
original file is always copied unchanged into `originals/`.

## Audit trail

Every action (`import`, `code_add`, `coding_add`, `export`, `backup`, ...) is
written to the `events` table with a UTC timestamp. `qda_export("audit")`
exports it as CSV -- ready to cite in the methods section: *"All coding
decisions were logged without gaps."*

## Offline guarantee

jellyqda never opens a network connection. The test suite scans the package
source for network calls and runs a full coding session as a regression test.
